parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: M1: find the scalar product of adjacent sides, e.g. OA·OC = 15 − 8 − 7. A1: show adjacent sides are perpendicular, with numerator working; without scalar-product calculation maximum M1 A1. M1: compare opposite sides, e.g. OA and CB or OC and AB. A1: show they are parallel and equal in length and conclude rectangle; e.g. AB = AO + OB = 3i + 4j − 7k = OC. If AB = OC is shown, award M1 A1 because parallelism and equal length follow. If only equal lengths are shown, M1; repeating for the other opposite pair earns A1. Alternative: show equal diagonals OB and AC (both length √104), show they bisect at (4,1,−3), establish a parallelogram and show adjacent sides perpendicular. [Total: 4]

Show the diagonals $\overrightarrow{OB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ are equal, both of length $\sqrt{104}$
Show the diagonals bisect at $(4,1,-3)$ and hence establish a parallelogram

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: B1: AC = ±(−2i + 6j − 8k), or ±(−i + 3j − 4k)/2 as used. M1: scalar product of relevant vectors, e.g. AC·OB = −16 + 12 + 48. M1: divide by the product of moduli and take inverse cosine, e.g. cos⁻¹(±44/104). A1: 65.0°, accept 1.13 radians. Alternative: M1 scalar product of a side and diagonal, e.g. OA·OB = 40 − 4 − 6 or OC·OB = 24 + 8 + 42; M1 correct modulus/inverse-cosine method; B1 use 180° − 2 × 57.5° or 180° − 2 × 32.5° and complete the acute-angle method; A1 65.0°. [Total: 4]

steps.working: scalar product of relevant vectors, e.g. $AC\cdot OB = -16 + 12 + 48$
divide by the product of moduli and take inverse cosine, e.g. $\cos^{-1}(\pm 44/104)$
Use the scalar product of a side and diagonal, e.g. $\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}=40-4-6$ or $\overrightarrow{OC}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}=24+8+42$
Use the correct modulus and inverse-cosine method
Use $180^\circ-2(57.5^\circ)$ or $180^\circ-2(32.5^\circ)$ and complete the acute-angle method
